checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch validate cell_index bounds BEFORE passing to coset_for_cell and coset_shift_for_cell?

state_context: Guard: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index >= params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns (runtime value=128). c-kzg-4844 CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128. The guard uses a runtime config value, not the C library compile-time constant. Validation flow: validateDataColumn -> verifier.ValidFields() [calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar, checks Index < NumberOfColumns] -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs [uses sidecar.Index as cell_index]. Two separate calls with no atomic invariant.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The cell_index passed to VerifyCellKZGProofBatch is sourced directly from sidecar.Index (uint64, P2P-controlled). VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns (128). The abstract domain is [0, 127]. NumberOfColumns is a runtime parameter, not a compile-time constant. The guard uses params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns which equals 128 = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB in current mainnet config — but this equality is unenforced. The Go-level VerifyCellKZGProofBatch does no independent bounds check on cellIndices before passing to the C library via CGO. The C library is the sole enforcer of index validity within its own domain.
state_anomalies_found: Guard uses runtime config value (params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns) not c-kzg-4844 compile-time constant (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128). Config drift could allow indices >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB to pass the guard.
VerifyDataColumnSidecar (ValidFields) and VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs (KZG verification) are called in separate function calls with no atomic invariant enforcement between them.
Current deployment: NumberOfColumns=128 == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128. No mismatch. Guard is practically tight.

Reconstruction path (reconstruction.go) uses map keys as cellIndices without going through VerifyDataColumnSidecar. If a sidecar column arrives via req/resp or reconstruction with arbitrary index, it bypasses the guard entirely.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For the normal attack path with current config: sidecar.Index must satisfy Index < 128 after ValidFields. This value is passed as cell_index to the C library. NumberOfColumns==CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB==128 means no out-of-bounds index reaches the C library via gossip. The vulnerability materializes under config drift or via non-gossip paths.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: Config drift scenario: NumberOfColumns configured to 256 (future upgrade or misconfiguration). Attacker sends sidecar with Index=200. VerifyDataColumnSidecar: 200 < 256 — PASSES. kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch receives cellIndex=200, which exceeds CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128. C library behavior for index >= 128 is implementation-defined — may return error, false, or access invalid memory.
attack_scenarios: Config drift: operator misconfigures NumberOfColumns > 128. Attacker sends sidecar with Index in (128, NumberOfColumns-1). Guard passes. C library receives out-of-bounds cell_index.
Non-gossip path bypass: reconstruction.go or req/resp handler calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs without prior VerifyDataColumnSidecar. Arbitrary sidecar.Index reaches C library.
Future upgrade: network upgrade increases CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB but Go guard not updated atomically — deployment window.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing-dependent exploit for primary scenario. Config-drift scenario requires misconfiguration, not a race.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Gossip path is the primary attack surface. Under current config (NumberOfColumns=128==CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB), the guard is tight. Non-gossip paths (reconstruction, req/resp) have weaker or absent guards.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant 'cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before KZG call' is enforced by VerifyDataColumnSidecar checking Index < NumberOfColumns (runtime=128 == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Proof holds ONLY if NumberOfColumns is invariably equal to CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. This equality is an unenforced assumption with no compile-time or init-time assertion. Additionally, the reconstruction path bypasses this guard.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient in general. Guard is correct only when params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns == ckzg4844.CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. No compile-time or runtime assertion enforces this equality. The reconstruction path bypasses the guard entirely.
edge_cases: Reconstruction path directly uses column map keys as cellIndices without VerifyDataColumnSidecar guard
Non-gossip ingest paths that call VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs without ValidFields

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The guard correctness depends on a non-enforced equality between a runtime config parameter and a C library compile-time constant. Any misconfiguration or version skew creates a direct path to passing an out-of-bounds index to a CGO C library with potentially undefined behavior. The reconstruction path bypasses the guard entirely. This is a defense-in-depth gap with a concrete exploit scenario.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: 1. Replace `params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns` guard with `ckzg4844.CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB` constant, or add an init-time assertion that both values are equal. 2. Add index bounds check in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs itself (application-level secondary check). 3. Add guard in reconstruction path before computing cellIndices from map keys.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can integer overflow in FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index bypass bounds checking or cause unexpected array access?

state_context: FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL=4096 (BytesPerCell/32=131072/32). cell_index uint64 bounded to [0,127] by guard. 4096*127=520192 — well within uint64 and C size_t. count += len(sidecar.Column) accumulation bounded by SSZ max_blob_commitments.size=4096. Go int is 64-bit on all target platforms.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: In Go code, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index is NOT performed. The Go layer passes uint64 cellIndices directly to the C library via CGO. The multiplication coset = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index is performed inside c-kzg-4844 C code. With cell_index bounded to [0,127] and FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL=4096, the product is at most 520192 — no overflow possible in uint64 or size_t. The count accumulation in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs uses Go int (64-bit on target platforms) and SSZ-bounded inputs (max 4096 per sidecar).
state_anomalies_found: No FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index multiplication exists in Go. The multiplication is inside the C library.
count += len(sidecar.Column): on 64-bit Go, overflow requires 2^63/4096 ≈ 2.25e15 concurrent sidecars — physically impossible.
Maximum product: 4096 * 127 = 520192 — trivially safe for all integer types.
No overflow risk exists in the current implementation at the Go layer.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index overflow in Go: not applicable — the multiplication does not exist in Go. For the C library: cell_index <= 127, product 4096*127=520192, no overflow. For count accumulation: 64-bit Go int, SSZ-bounded input, no overflow.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: No integer overflow constructible for FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index in Go code — the computation does not exist in Go. The C library receives bounded inputs (cell_index <= 127). The product 4096 * 127 = 520192 cannot overflow any standard integer type.
attack_scenarios: Only theoretical: if CHK-0111 config-drift scenario is triggered AND cell_index = UINT64_MAX reaches C library, C unsigned arithmetic wraps: 4096 * UINT64_MAX mod 2^64 = large value accessing wrong coset. This is a follow-on from CHK-0111, not an independent vulnerability.
32-bit Go platform with many sidecars: int overflow in count. Requires ~2^31/4096 = 524288 concurrent sidecars, unrealistic.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No integer overflow at the Go layer for this computation. The C library receives bounded, guarded inputs. The only theoretical overflow requires chaining with CHK-0111 and is limited to 32-bit platforms or pathological configurations.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'no integer overflow in FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index' holds trivially in Go because the multiplication is not performed in Go. In the C library, the invariant holds because cell_index <= 127 is enforced by the guard, and 4096 * 127 = 520192 does not overflow any integer type. The proof is successful for the current implementation.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: VerifyDataColumnSidecar: Index < numberOfColumns (128) ensures cell_index <= 127; SSZ max constraint limits Column length to max_blob_commitments.size (4096)
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. No Go-level multiplication exists. C library receives bounded inputs. Count accumulation is 64-bit bounded.
edge_cases: 32-bit Go deployment with massive concurrent sidecars (unrealistic)
C library overflow if cell_index guard bypassed (chained from CHK-0111)

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No integer overflow exists in the Go code for FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index because this multiplication does not exist in Go. The C library receives inputs bounded to [0,127] by the guard. 4096 * 127 = 520192 cannot overflow any integer type used in modern C or Go. The count accumulation is bounded by SSZ constraints on 64-bit platforms.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No action required for this specific check. If CHK-0111's config-drift risk is addressed, this item remains safe.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Are commitment_bytes, cell, and proof_bytes lengths validated to exact constants before processing in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

state_context: SSZ decoder is the sole enforcer of per-element byte lengths. VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks count equality only, not per-element byte sizes. kzg.Bytes48=[48]byte, kzg.Cell=[131072]byte. Go 1.20+ slice-to-fixed-array conversion panics if len(slice) < array_size. Any bypass of SSZ decoder or non-SSZ path (RPC, reconstruction, DB load) reaches panic.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: At trust boundary tb-002 (P2P gossip), SSZ decoding enforces kzg_commitments[i]=48 bytes, kzg_proofs[i]=48 bytes, column[i]=131072 bytes. The Go type conversions kzg.Bytes48() and kzg.Cell() perform fixed-size array conversions from []byte. In Go 1.20+, slice-to-fixed-array conversion panics if len(slice) < target array size. Application code (VerifyDataColumnSidecar) checks only COUNT equality between Column, KzgCommitments, and KzgProofs — not per-element byte lengths. The sole per-element length enforcement is the SSZ decoder.
state_anomalies_found: Go runtime panic: kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i]) panics if len(KzgCommitments[i]) < 48
Go runtime panic: kzg.Cell(sidecar.Column[i]) panics if len(Column[i]) < 131072
Go runtime panic: kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgProofs[i]) panics if len(KzgProofs[i]) < 48
VerifyDataColumnSidecar does NOT check per-element byte lengths — only count equality
SSZ decoder is the single enforcement point — any bypass or bug exposes runtime panic

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Attack path: malicious peer sends DataColumnSidecar with KzgCommitments[0] length=32. SSZ decoder SHOULD reject. IF SSZ decoder has bug or non-SSZ path is used, VerifyDataColumnSidecar passes (count equality check), and kzg.Bytes48() panics.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: 1. Internal API or test creates DataColumnSidecar with KzgCommitments[0]=make([]byte,32). 2. Calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs directly. 3. VerifyDataColumnSidecar passes (count check: len(Column)==len(KzgCommitments)==1). 4. kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgCommitments[0]) panics: 'runtime error: cannot convert slice with length 32 to array or pointer to array with length 48'. 5. If recover() absent: process crash (DoS).
attack_scenarios: SSZ decoder bug: malformed gossip message with short commitment bytes bypasses length enforcement. Application panics.
Non-gossip ingest path (RPC, import, reconstruction) constructs sidecar with wrong-length commitment bytes. Application panics.
Gossip flooding: high-frequency malformed messages causing SSZ decode + reject overhead (resource exhaustion even if safely rejected).
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency. Panic is deterministic given wrong-length input.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Primary attack surface: P2P gossip (SSZ-guarded). Secondary: internal API, RPC, reconstruction paths (not SSZ-guarded). Application-level code has no secondary length check on individual commitment_bytes, proof_bytes, or cell bytes.
entry_points: P2P gossip: decodePubsubMessage -> SSZ decode -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs
Internal calls: reconstruction.go -> operations without SSZ decode

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant 'commitment_bytes length == 48 at point of kzg.Bytes48() conversion' enforced exclusively by SSZ decoding. NO Go-level check in VerifyDataColumnSidecar, VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs, or VerifyCellKZGProofBatch for per-element byte lengths. Proof succeeds only if SSZ decoding is perfectly enforced — a single point of trust with no defense-in-depth.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SSZ decoder enforcing ssz_size='?,48' for kzg_commitments and kzg_proofs, ssz_size='?,bytes_per_cell.size' for column (in gossip path only)
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient at application layer. SSZ decoder is single point of trust. Any bypass, bug, or non-SSZ path exposes runtime panics. No defense-in-depth.
edge_cases: SSZ decoder bug in Prysm's fastssz library for repeated fixed-size bytes fields
Non-SSZ ingest path: block import, database read, internal test construction
Reconstruction path (reconstruction.go): directly uses sidecar.Column[blobIndex] as kzg.Cell with no length check
Go runtime panic recovery behavior depends on pubsub library version

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Application-level code has no secondary validation of commitment_bytes, proof_bytes, or cell byte lengths before unsafe type conversions. The sole enforcement is SSZ decoding. Any SSZ decoder weakness or non-gossip path exposes runtime panic (DoS). The reconstruction path is particularly vulnerable as it directly converts Column[blobIndex] to kzg.Cell without any length check. This is a concrete missing defense-in-depth at a security boundary.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Add explicit length validation in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs before type conversions: for each i, require len(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i])==48, len(sidecar.KzgProofs[i])==48, len(sidecar.Column[i])==kzg.BytesPerCell (131072). Return error on violation. Also add in reconstruction.go before kzg.Cell() conversion.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer send commitment_bytes with incorrect length to cause crash or memory corruption?

state_context: kzg.Bytes48=[48]byte. Conversion from []byte to [48]byte panics in Go 1.20+ if len(slice) < 48. VerifyDataColumnSidecar does NOT check len(KzgCommitments[i]). SSZ decoder is the only enforcement. pubsub goroutine panic recovery depends on go-libp2p-pubsub version. A panic that reaches the goroutine boundary without recover() crashes the process.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: A malicious P2P peer sends a gossip message with commitment_bytes of incorrect length. The message flows through SSZ decoding (guard) before reaching application code. If SSZ decoding correctly enforces element size = 48 bytes, the message is rejected before any application code runs. If SSZ decoding has a bug or non-SSZ path is used, the short commitment reaches kzg.Bytes48() and causes a runtime panic in Go 1.20+.
state_anomalies_found: kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i]) panics if len(KzgCommitments[i]) < 48 — Go 1.20+ behavior
VerifyDataColumnSidecar has NO per-element length check for commitment_bytes
SSZ is the sole enforcement layer — single point of trust
A panic in gossip validator goroutine MAY crash the process depending on go-libp2p-pubsub version's recover() usage

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Primary attack path requires SSZ decoder bypass. If bypassed: commitment_bytes with len=32 passes ValidFields (count check), kzg.Bytes48() panics, potential node crash. The attack is directly realizable via internal APIs without SSZ decoding.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: 1. Attacker (internal caller or compromised path) constructs DataColumnSidecar proto with KzgCommitments[0]=make([]byte,32). 2. Calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs directly (bypassing SSZ). 3. ValidFields passes (count check: 1==1). 4. Loop body: kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgCommitments[0]) -> panic 'cannot convert slice with length 32 to array or pointer to array with length 48'. 5. If pubsub validator has no recover(): process crash. If SSZ decoder has bug: same outcome from gossip path.
attack_scenarios: SSZ decoder bug: attacker sends malformed gossip message with 32-byte commitment. If SSZ decoder passes it through, application panics.
Internal API: any internal path that constructs DataColumnSidecar with wrong-length commitments and calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs without SSZ decode.
Reconnaissance: attacker probes by sending various commitment lengths to enumerate decoder behavior before crafting exploit.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency. Panic is deterministic given wrong-length input.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Reachable from P2P gossip (conditional on SSZ decoder bug) and directly from internal APIs (unconditional). The gossip path is the primary external attack surface.
entry_points: P2P gossip subscriber: validateDataColumn in beacon-chain/sync/validate_data_column.go
Internal APIs: any code calling VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs without prior SSZ decoding

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant 'KzgCommitments[i] has length 48 when reaching kzg.Bytes48()' is enforced by SSZ decoder alone. Application code (VerifyDataColumnSidecar) checks count equality only — not per-element byte lengths. The invariant proof fails because there is no application-level enforcement.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SSZ decoder: ssz_size='?,48' for kzg_commitments (gossip path only). No application-level guard.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient. No application-level length check for individual KzgCommitments[i] elements. ValidFields only checks count equality. A malformed SSZ message that bypasses decoder enforcement reaches a panic.
edge_cases: SSZ decoder version with a bug in repeated fixed-size bytes parsing
Prysm upgrade that changes SSZ library without retesting length enforcement
Message arrived via non-gossip path (RPC, import) without SSZ decoding

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Sending commitment_bytes with incorrect length is a plausible attack scenario. If SSZ decoder has any weakness (single enforcement point), the application code panics via Go's unsafe fixed-array conversion, potentially crashing the node. The application has no secondary length check — a missing defense-in-depth layer. Even if SSZ is correct today, any refactoring or SSZ library change could expose this.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: In VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs, add: for each i, if len(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i]) != 48 { return fmt.Errorf("commitment %d has length %d, expected 48", i, len(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i])) }. Similarly for KzgProofs and Column.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer send cell with incorrect length to cause crash or memory corruption?
checklist_item.bug_class: Buffer Overflow via Malformed Cell Length

state_context: kzg.Cell=[131072]byte. Go 1.20+ panics if slice length < 131072 on conversion to fixed array. SSZ enforces bytes_per_cell.size=131072 in gossip path. Reconstruction path bypasses SSZ — no guard. Oversized cell (len > 131072) causes silent truncation in Go (copy semantics) — first 131072 bytes used, trailing bytes ignored. Short cell causes panic. BYTES_PER_CELL=131072=FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL*BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT=4096*32.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: A malicious P2P peer sends DataColumnSidecar with cell data of incorrect length (< 131072 bytes or > 131072 bytes). SSZ enforces exact size in gossip path. Application code has no per-element length check. kzg.Cell(sidecar.Column[i]) panics if len < 131072. Oversized cell causes silent truncation (attacker controls first 131072 bytes). The reconstruction path is an additional direct vulnerability: it calls kzg.Cell(cell) where cell = sidecar.Column[blobIndex] with NO length check and NO SSZ decoding in that path.
state_anomalies_found: kzg.Cell(sidecar.Column[i]) panics if len(Column[i]) < 131072 — no application-level check prevents this
Reconstruction path: kzg.Cell(cell) where cell=sidecar.Column[blobIndex] — NO length check, NO SSZ enforcement — DIRECTLY VULNERABLE
VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks count equality only, not per-element cell byte lengths
Oversized cell (len > 131072): Go silently uses first 131072 bytes — attacker can deliver crafted cell content that passes structural length checks
SSZ annotation ssz_size='?,bytes_per_cell.size' is enforced at decode time only, not application time

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Short cell panic (gossip path): requires SSZ decoder bypass. Short cell panic (reconstruction path): directly reachable without SSZ — any sidecar loaded from DB or received via req/resp with Column[i] length < 131072 panics in reconstruction. Oversized cell: requires SSZ decoder bug, but if present attacker controls cell content reaching C library.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: Reconstruction path exploit (no SSZ required): 1. Node receives a data column sidecar via req/resp protocol (not gossip). 2. Sidecar is stored to database or used directly. 3. Reconstruction code at reconstruction.go line ~81: cells = append(cells, kzg.Cell(cell)) where cell = sidecar.Column[blobIndex]. 4. sidecar.Column[blobIndex] has length 100 bytes (malformed). 5. kzg.Cell() conversion panics: 'cannot convert slice with length 100 to array or pointer to array with length 131072'. 6. If panic propagates: node crash (DoS). Gossip path: same outcome if SSZ decoder has element-size enforcement bug.
attack_scenarios: Reconstruction path panic (no SSZ bypass needed): malformed sidecar from req/resp with short Column[blobIndex]. Direct DoS via reconstruction code.
Gossip path panic (requires SSZ decoder bug): malformed gossip message with short cell bytes bypasses SSZ enforcement.
Oversized cell data smuggling: attacker sends cell with trailing garbage bytes. If SSZ incorrectly accepts variable-size element, attacker controls first 131072 bytes passed to c-kzg-4844.
Database corruption: if database read does not revalidate cell lengths, a corrupted DB entry with short cells causes panic during reconstruction.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency. Panic is deterministic per-call.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The reconstruction path (beacon-chain/core/peerdas/reconstruction.go) is directly reachable without SSZ enforcement and has no length check before kzg.Cell() conversion. This is a concrete code-level vulnerability independent of SSZ decoder behavior. The gossip path is conditionally reachable via SSZ decoder bugs.
entry_points: Req/resp protocol: data column sidecar by range/root requests (may not have same SSZ element-size enforcement)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: The reconstruction path is directly exploitable. Any attacker that can cause the node to receive and store a malformed sidecar (with short Column elements) via req/resp can trigger a panic in the reconstruction code path.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant 'Column[i] has length 131072 when reaching kzg.Cell()' is enforced by SSZ decoding in the gossip path ONLY. The reconstruction path has NO enforcement — the invariant is trivially falsifiable for this path. For the gossip path, the invariant holds only if SSZ decoder is bug-free — single point of trust. Proof fails for reconstruction path.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SSZ decoder (gossip path only). NO guard exists in reconstruction path before kzg.Cell() conversion.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient. Reconstruction path: direct absence of length validation — provably vulnerable. Gossip path: relies on SSZ decoder alone — no application-level defense-in-depth.
edge_cases: Reconstruction path: sidecar.Column[blobIndex] conversion to kzg.Cell with no length check — concrete code-level vulnerability
Req/resp protocol path: may have different SSZ enforcement rules for element sizes
Database-loaded sidecars with corrupted column bytes
Silent truncation for oversized cells if SSZ accepts variable element sizes

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The reconstruction path in beacon-chain/core/peerdas/reconstruction.go directly converts sidecar.Column[blobIndex] to kzg.Cell without any length check. This is a concrete observable code vulnerability: if a malformed sidecar with a short Column element reaches this path (via req/resp, database, or internal construction), the node panics. This is directly reachable without requiring SSZ decoder bypass. The gossip path additionally lacks application-level defense-in-depth. Both represent real security gaps.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: 1. In VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs (p2p_interface.go lines 73-79): add before each type conversion — for each i: if len(sidecar.Column[i]) != kzg.BytesPerCell { return fmt.Errorf(...) }, if len(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i]) != 48 { return fmt.Errorf(...) }, if len(sidecar.KzgProofs[i]) != 48 { return fmt.Errorf(...) }. 2. In reconstruction.go: add len(cell) == kzg.BytesPerCell check before kzg.Cell(cell) conversion. 3. Consider centralizing per-element byte length validation into VerifyDataColumnSidecar so all paths benefit.
